text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Workers at the international airport Otopeni threaten to launch strike and ground flights.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea asked parliament to endorse his cabinet's tough reform programme.
- The Netherlands ranks first on the list of foreign investors in Romania.
- The World Bank will give Romania a $2.5 million credit to upgrade the irrigation system across the country.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Trade unions at the Romtelecom SA telephone operator threaten to launch national strike to protest against the company's failure to sign the collective labour contract.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Finance Ministry said financial bottlenecks in the economy amount to some 7.7 trillion lei.
- The government plans steps to delay increases of fuel prices.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- U.S. President Bill Clinton wrote to Romanian President Emil Constantinescu to congratulate him on the signing of the treaty with Ukraine, saying the treaty was an important contribution to European stability.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Bucharest court of appeals has sentenced Marcel Ivan, former president of troubled private bank Credit Bank, to six years in jail for embezzlement, fraud and forgery.

- Ex-president Ion Iliescu, leader of the opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), slammed PDSR deputy and his former campaign manager Iosif Boda for attacking the party's executive leader Adrian Nastase in the party's first internal row.
ADEVARUL

- Romania's largest trade union federations plan a series of protests next week to criticise the government for what they call the government's lack of coherence in reforms and failure to communicate with the unions.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The PDSR is confronted with a political crisis.
- Only 25 percent of Bucharest residents who travel on public transport buy tickets, Constantin Popescu, the head of Bucharest local transport authority said in an interview.
- Popescu said the state is subsidising some 40 percent of the cost of a trip with the public transport in the capital. ($ = 7,142 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
